transcript.note: Round 1. The straightening left 64 of 74 segments H/V and 72 of 74 within the eight directions, so there is essentially no alignment left to win and the whole value of this loop is in the grid. I counted what compaction can actually reach: the 60x60 field holds only 19 distinct occupied columns and 22 distinct occupied rows, and compactGridSafe removes empty bands but cannot merge two occupied ones - that has to be done by moving vertices, which is what this round does. I looked for bands holding one or two vertices whose every incident segment is perpendicular to the merge direction, so the merge is free. Columns: 47 and 11 both vacate column 22 for column 29 (both keep their horizontals; 47 must stay west of 4, so 4 steps on to column 31 rather than 29 and vacates column 30 in the process), 29 to column 31, 0 to column 40, and 32/55 translate together from column 59 to 54 keeping 55-32 vertical - five columns down to fourteen. 0 is a special case: it cannot go further west than column 40 even though columns 29-36 are occupied, because its horizontal to 20 would then cross the long column-36 vertical 35-45 at row 13; column 40 is the westernmost occupied column that clears the spine. Rows: 5 and 6 move up to row 7 to fold row 8 into the existing north-west row, 37 to row 7, the 53/54 pair to row 18, 48 to row 20, 42 to row 33, 19 to row 49 and 56 to row 52 - seven rows down to fifteen. I deliberately left row 40 alone: 26 is the only vertex there, but its diagonal to 27 needs exactly a three-row gap, and no other occupied row is three from 27's, so merging it would cost a 45 deg segment and the batch would rightly be rejected for a lower score. Every move here keeps a vertex inside its quadrant relative to all neighbours and leaves both counts untouched at 64/72; the gain is a grid roughly 19x22 to 14x15 of occupied bands, plus visibly shorter stubs on 0, 46, 19 and 32.

Round 2. Compaction is rank-based, so re-reading the layout in the new 14x15 coordinates is not cosmetic - four segments that were exact 45 deg in the old 60x60 field are no longer diagonal there (the eight-direction count reads 68, not 72), and conversely 23-20, which I had written off as permanently stuck during the straightening, has landed on an exact diagonal for free. That means the useful work now is whatever the tightened grid newly allows. The one real opening is the 26-27 pair: 26 is alone on row 9 and 27/28 alone on row 10, one row apart with a two-column offset. Rather than pull 26 down to make it 45 deg, I lift 27 and 28 up onto 26's row, which turns 26-27 into a true horizontal - H/V beats 45 deg - and empties row 10 all the same, so I get the band merge and the alignment from a single move instead of choosing between them. 28 rides along because 27-28 is horizontal and must stay so; both stay inside their quadrants (27 lands exactly on 26's row, which the rule permits, and stays below 19). I checked the lengthened verticals 28-51 and 27-19 pass through no vertex at the vacated row, and that the new horizontal 26-27 clears 39-42, which stops one row short of it. I also pulled the terminal 46 in from column 13 to 12 - it changes no band count but shortens the longest remaining stub on the eastern edge, which is the loop's fourth objective. I deliberately did not move 42 into the freed row: it is the only thing holding row 8, but the only cell available to it there sits underneath the new 26-27 horizontal and would be swallowed by it.

Convergence note (no moves). Two rounds took the grid from 60x60 to 14x14 of occupied bands and H/V from 64 to 65 of 74. I went through every remaining band and every remaining unaligned segment to check there is a third round worth running, and there is not. Bands: each surviving single-vertex band is pinned by the quadrant rule to exactly one index - 21 must stay below 6, 52 above 49, 50 between 51 and 49, 34 between 17 and 55, 4 between 47 and 35, 47 between 8 and 4, 39 between 16 and 25 - so they cannot merge with a neighbouring band at all. The two interesting near-misses both fail on the same obstacle: column 9 (vertices 2 and 3) could fold into column 10, but their vertical would then swallow 5, which itself cannot leave row 1 or move west without being swallowed by 6-5; and rows 8 and 9 could fold together, but 42 sits at column 7 exactly between 26 and 27, so the merged horizontal would swallow it, while 42 cannot escape downward either because its own vertical would then cross that horizontal. I measured that one: 63/67, correctly worse. Segments: the five still unaligned are 45-20, 36-23, 44-58, 13-38 and 38-12. 44-58, 36-23 and 38-12 have both endpoints locked on both axes by intersecting H and V segments; 13-38 has a fixed three-column offset and 38 cannot leave row 3 (it is boxed between 18 and 23); 45-20 is the only one with a free axis, and both of its options are dead ends - row 2 makes it a true H but the segment would swallow 0, which cannot move aside because every column west of it puts its own horizontal across the column-4 spine, and row 4 makes it 45 deg at the exact cost of the 45 deg on 45-36, which I measured as 65/69, unchanged. So the layout is at a fixed point on both objectives. Stopping at round 2 of the 10 allowed.
